docs.title: Documentation
docs.lead: Get LocaleDesk running and through your first localization pass.
docs.reqBody: macOS 13.0 or later. For iOS string catalogs, Xcode 15+ is recommended on the machine that consumes the output.
docs.getBody: Install LocaleDesk from the Mac App Store. Launch once, then open Settings if you want to connect your own translation service endpoint.
docs.step1: Choose a platform: iOS, Flutter, or Electron.
docs.step2: Select the source file and output location, then pick target languages.
docs.step3: Start conversion. Open Review to check results, export CSV, or sync back.
docs.formatsBody: LocaleDesk works with iOS .strings / .xcstrings (String Catalog), Flutter .arb, and Electron localized .json.
docs.faqTeaser: Common questions about formats, API keys, and Review.
docs.faq1Q: Can I skip strings that already have translations?
docs.faq1A: Yes. Enable “Skip existing translations” so only missing keys are generated.
docs.faq2A: Review is a table of keys and locales so you can verify, filter missing rows, and export before shipping.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.lead: Answers for developers evaluating LocaleDesk for iOS, Flutter, and Electron localization on Mac.
faq.a1: LocaleDesk is a macOS app for batch-localizing app string files. Convert source locales into target languages, review the results, then export or sync back into your project.
faq.a2: iOS .strings and .xcstrings (String Catalog), Flutter .arb, and Electron localized .json files.
faq.q3: Do I need an API key?
faq.a3: Only if you want AI-assisted translation through your own provider account (bring your own key). LocaleDesk does not sell API keys and does not run a translation marketplace.
faq.a4: You can run LocaleDesk without Xcode. If your iOS project uses String Catalogs, Xcode 15+ is recommended on the machine that consumes the exported .xcstrings.
faq.q5: Does localization stay on my Mac?
faq.a5: Files you open stay under your control on your device unless you explicitly send them to a third-party service you configure. See the Privacy page for details.
faq.q7: How is this different from spreadsheets or editing String Catalog alone?
faq.a7: Spreadsheets lose structure and are easy to desync. Editing one catalog by hand does not scale across many locales. LocaleDesk keeps file structure, batch-generates missing locales, and gives you a Review table before you ship.
faq.a8: From the Mac App Store. Use the download button on this site or search for LocaleDesk on the store.
faq.cta: Download on the Mac App Store

xcstrings.title: Batch-localize .xcstrings on Mac
xcstrings.lead: LocaleDesk helps iOS teams translate and review String Catalog (.xcstrings) files without spreadsheet chaos.
xcstrings.pWhat: Apple’s String Catalog format (.xcstrings) stores keys, comments, and per-locale translations in one structured file. It replaced many .strings / .stringsdict workflows for modern Xcode projects—and it grows quickly once you add languages.
xcstrings.pProblem: Hand-editing catalogs for every locale is slow and error-prone. Exporting to spreadsheets often drops comments, plural rules, or key structure. Teams need a Mac-native loop: pick targets, fill missing translations, review, then write back.
xcstrings.li1: Convert — choose iOS / String Catalog, select target languages, generate missing locales in one pass.
xcstrings.li2: Review — inspect keys and translations in a table; filter gaps before they hit your repo.
xcstrings.li3: Export or sync — keep structure suitable for Xcode projects that consume .xcstrings.
xcstrings.pWho: Indie Mac/iOS developers and small teams shipping multilingual apps who already use String Catalogs—or are moving from .strings to .xcstrings and need a practical batch workflow on macOS.
xcstrings.pAlso: The same Convert → Review flow also supports Flutter .arb and Electron localized .json, so multi-stack teams can stay in one tool.
xcstrings.cta: Download on the Mac App Store

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: LocaleDesk is designed to keep your localization work on your Mac.
privacy.s1Body: The Mac app does not require a LocaleDesk account. Localization files you open stay under your control on your device unless you explicitly send them to a third-party service you configure.
privacy.s2Body: If you enter an API key for a third-party AI or translation provider, requests go to that provider under your account. LocaleDesk does not sell API keys and does not operate those services.
privacy.s3Body: Purchases and downloads through the Mac App Store are handled by Apple under Apple’s privacy policy.
privacy.s4Body: For privacy questions about this app, use the support contact listed on the Mac App Store product page.
